text:
maya: heads-up — privacy team ran a manual DSAR delete for user X this morning and we saw a big spike in service-account access logs. can we triage?
liam: saw that too. looks like the delete-job used sa:dsar-cleaner-v2 which recently got expanded perms. suspect RBAC change.
anika: copying the DSAR ticket here. requester needed full delete + proof. we ran backfilled deletes across embeddings + backups.
sam: logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-17T09:12:03Z sa:dsar-cleaner-v2 GET /embeddings?user=X 200 120ms
2026-03-17T09:12:04Z sa:dsar-cleaner-v2 DELETE /embeddings/rows?filter=user:X 202 1.2s
2026-03-17T09:12:05Z sa:dsar-cleaner-v2 LIST /kms/keys - 200
```
liam: important line is LIST /kms/keys — cleaner shouldn't be able to enumerate customer keys. that was part of the new role binding.
maya: is this currently a vulnerability or more of a policy breach? we need to classify for incident response.
liam: depends — if cleaner can enumerate keys, it could potentially identify key IDs tied to customers. low-severity info exposure but definitely not allowed. flagged in vuln-scan yesterday: CVE-like tag "RBAC-PRIV-2026-02"
anika: legal asks for proof-of-deletion and metadata audit. if we roll back perms it might break generating proof. need a plan that preserves ability to verify deletes without extra surface area.
sam: proposal: split responsibilities — dsar-cleaner gets explicit delete/write on resource namespaces for user objects, but move any KMS operations to a new service sa:dsar-kms-proxy with limited HSM-wrapped key access and explicit allowlist for key ids. dsar-cleaner calls the proxy via mTLS.
maya: agree. also add an audit hook — every delete must emit an immutable audit event to the internal audit-log topic (signed). Legal needs retention of that proof for 30d after DSAR.
liam: technical tasks: 1) revert the recent role change on sa:dsar-cleaner-v2 (PR #846) asap 2) create sa:dsar-kms-proxy with scoped perms 3) update deletion pipeline to call proxy over internal API 4) add audit signer and sink to s3-retention-bucket:gs-audit (immutable)
sam: I can open the rollback PR and emergency ACL patch now.
maya: @sam please include a short rollback checklist in the PR description and tag oncall.
ops-bot: deploy-batch: started rollout dsar-cleaner-v2-rollback to prod at 2026-03-17T09:20:00Z
liam: also: backups were touched per anika. we need an exception path for backups that are on the retention schedule. can't fully delete backups without legal signoff. that needs to be reflected in the DSAR runbook.
anika: confirmed. we documented retention exceptions: cloud-backups/* have a legal_hold tag. for this DSAR we only removed active store copies and marked backup records for legal review.
maya: two governance actions: update DSAR runbook with backup exception steps, and create an RBAC pre-merge bot rule that blocks grants that add kms:ListKeys or iam:ListServiceAccounts to dsar-related service accounts.
sam: quick mitigation pushed: denied iam:ListServiceAccounts for sa:dsar-cleaner-v2 and removed kms:ListKeys. monitoring alert created: sec.dsar.unexpected-kms-list -> pages on repeat within 5m.
liam: follow-ups: schedule KMS policy review with infra + security (tomorrow 10am), implement allowlist for KMS key ids, and add HSM-backed key use only via dsar-kms-proxy.
anika: legal wants export of audit trail for this DSAR (ids + SignedDeleteProof). can we produce that from current logs?
maya: yes — we'll produce a SignedDeleteProof bundle. format is: {user_id, objects_deleted[], timestamp, signer_id, signature}. I'll generate and ship to legal by EOD.
sam: vuln-triage: mark RBAC-PRIV-2026-02 as "remediated by rollback + proxy design". will attach PRs and audit.
maya: update incident channel and postmortem checklist: record timeline, root cause (overbroad RBAC change in PR #846), mitigations, and runbook updates.
liam: adding action items to ticket: ACTION-1 rollback PR, ACTION-2 create dsar-kms-proxy, ACTION-3 audit hook, ACTION-4 runbook update, ACTION-5 legal deliverable.
anika: thanks — legal will standby for the SignedDeleteProof and backup exception notes.
maya: nice work team. once PRs are merged let's do a short blameless postmortem and close the DSAR ticket. :thumbsup:
